distinguishing_features: Uses spatial pressure differentials across individual cutterhead spokes rather than temporal transient analysis of a single baghouse ΔP signal
Detects early clay adhesion on cutterhead spokes before visible clogging rather than bag rupture via post-pulse transient asymmetry
Per-spoke geometric distribution signature (asymmetric resistance pattern) rather than a compartment-level collapse/transient identifier
Threshold based on cross-spoke ΔP shift magnitude (≥3 kPa) rather than SPC of cleaning-cycle transient baselines
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to detect incipient clay adhesion on a cutterhead before it becomes a visible blockage, using pressure telemetry as a leading indicator rather than a static absolute-pressure threshold alarm.
parsed.viable_reason: Per-spoke pressure transducers and computation-only inferencing are feasible and testable with a stated pass/fail protocol and detectable 2 kPa shift, though the 3 kPa threshold vs ±0.5 kPa sensor accuracy and 1-hour detection window are plausible as written.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: The closest prior art (baghouse ΔP) uses a single measured ΔP with temporal transient analysis, whereas the candidate invents a cross-spatial per-spoke differential signature for adhesion onset, which is not a routine parameter change of that approach.
